blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cypress Park Estates

District sources call the existing residential area Cypress Park, Rodgers Creek and the Uplands, plus the planned Cypress Village and Cypress West future neighbourhoods. It is also a different place from Cypress Provincial Park and from Cypress Mountain Resort, which sit up the same road (Cypress Bowl Road) and are not residential stock.
Where Cypress Park Estates sits
Drive time to Cypress Park Estates
Hawksley — 3963 Uplands Way on current MLS listings (District of West Vancouver)

A new condominium development by British Pacific Properties in collaboration with Beedie Living, in the Rodgers Creek / Uplands CD3 area (District Development Permit 24-106 covers 3900 Cypress Bowl Road, Area 5, Rodgers Creek). Current listings describe apartment/condo units at 3963 Uplands Way as freehold strata, concrete construction, built 2026, with amenities including a fitness centre, resident lounge, music room, bike workshop and dog wash station. Two source conflicts to flag: (1) ADDRESS — the presale source gives the project address as 3271–3281 Uplands Way, while current MLS listings for completed units use 3963 Uplands Way; not confirmed whether these are two phases of one project or a project-address vs civic-address difference — verify the civic address and strata plan for the specific unit. (2) COUNT — the presale source states 57 condominiums and 7 townhomes in a 10-storey building, a 6-storey building and a 2-storey townhouse podium, while another project source describes a 72-unit condominium building and a listing directory describes a "72 Unit Development"; the totals do not reconcile on the sources checked (57 + 7 = 64), so the unit count is not confirmed beyond "57 condominiums plus 7 townhomes per the presale source." Published restrictions: a listing directory states pets allowed for the building; rental and age restrictions are not confirmed from the sources checked. Because the building completed in 2026, some units may still be developer sales — GST and REDMA then apply.
Streets, schools and getting around Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Exact boundaries are not verified — District planning sources place the area above Highway 1, below the 1,200-foot contour, with the Rodgers Creek area east of Cypress Bowl Road and the Cypress Village planning area west of it.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: in exactly one building — Hawksley, on Uplands Way in the Rodgers Creek CD3 pocket. Everything else verified in the area is detached houses on RS2/RS3/RS5 streets, semi-detached strata homes, or future Cypress Village land west of Cypress Bowl Road that is not yet built stock.

Transit anchor: TransLink route 256 (Whitby Estates / Park Royal), a community shuttle, runs via Chippendale Road to Westhill at the edge of this area, then via 21st Street, Gordon Avenue, 22nd Street and Marine Drive to Park Royal. No TransLink route up Cypress Bowl Road to the ski area is documented in the timetables read; BC Parks states the resort runs a free shuttle between Lot 3B and the downhill and nordic areas in ski season. This is a car-based area.

Anchors: Cypress Falls Park, Cypress Trails Park and Woodburn Park are District parks in the area; District recreation (West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive) and the West Vancouver Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive) are in Ambleside, east and below the area; Cypress Park Primary (IB PYP, K–3) is at 4355 Marine Drive at the foot of the slope — named for the area but not a confirmed catchment school for an Upper Lands address.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Cypress Park Estates

items.t: District plans and zoning (West Vancouver — its own bylaws): the area sits under the District of West Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, and Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010.

Wildfire and watercourse permits — the defining checks on this slope: a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface, and the District's Community Wildfire Resiliency Plan describes the Cypress Park area as consistently sloped terrain. An Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank — Cypress Creek and Rodgers Creek both run through the area — and steep-terrain subdivisions can trigger a difficult-terrain permit. These apply to strata alterations and landscaping at Hawksley and Chippendale Mews, not just to house lots.

District tax timing: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. District water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Three Cypress names share one road. The residential pocket, Cypress Provincial Park and Cypress Mountain Resort are different places; a listing that trades on ski-hill proximity is describing a drive up Cypress Bowl Road, not a location inside the resort.

Rodgers Creek just roughly doubled on paper. A District-approved modification of the Rodgers Creek rezoning for Areas 5 and 6 raised the approved homes from 493 across 16 buildings to 974 across 17 buildings, lifted maximum heights from 12 storeys to 14 and up to 16 storeys on some sites, and added two 12-storey buildings with up to 280 purpose-built secured market rental homes combined, with a $7.14 million voluntary community amenity contribution from British Pacific Properties. Hawksley's buyers are buying into the first phase of a much larger build-out.

Cypress Village is approved and its first works are permitted. The Area Development Plan for Cypress Village and Eagleridge was approved by Council with Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024 creating the Cypress Village (CV) Zone; Development Permit 24-115 to British Pacific Properties Limited covers initial works (commenced January 2025), and the Eagleridge lands transferred to the District (262 acres) were dedicated as park in April 2025. The village's planned shopping, school and community centre are future amenities — do not price them as present.

The school locator literally has no answer for the sample address. 3900 Cypress Bowl Road falls outside the SD45 locator's listed ranges for Cypress Bowl Road (Even 3850–3850, Odd 3755–3757) — a listing that names a catchment school for an Upper Lands condo is stating something the district's own tool does not confirm.

The area's "primary school" is three grades, at the bottom of the hill. Cypress Park Primary is a K–3 IB PYP school at 4355 Marine Drive whose students have the opportunity to continue the IB programme at West Bay Elementary — it is not a full K–7 neighbourhood elementary for the Uplands, whatever a listing implies.

The new building's own numbers do not agree with each other yet. Hawksley appears as 57 condos + 7 townhomes in its presale source and as a 72-unit development in other project and listing sources, at two different Uplands Way addresses — early-days documentation for a 2026 building is exactly why the strata plan and disclosure/Form B, not marketing pages, govern a purchase here.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Cypress Park Estates

District sources call the existing residential area Cypress Park, Rodgers Creek and the Uplands, plus the planned Cypress Village and Cypress West future neighbourhoods. It is also a different place from Cypress Provincial Park and from Cypress Mountain Resort, which sit up the same road (Cypress Bowl Road) and are not residential stock. Both bases are stated in the entry; the count lives in British Properties alone. Municipality, stated first because it decides the bylaws: Cypress Park Estates is in the District of West Vancouver — OCP Bylaw No. 4985, 2018 / Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010. White Rock's Bylaw 2506 / 2220 pair belongs to White Rock only and is never imported here.
Streets, schools and getting around Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Exact boundaries are not verified as an exact line — District planning sources place the area above Highway 1, below the 1,200-foot contour, with the Rodgers Creek area east of Cypress Bowl Road and the Cypress Village planning area west of it. Nearby: Rodgers Creek and the British Properties / Chartwell (east and south-east), Whitby Estates and Westhill (south, below Highway 1), Caulfeild (south-west, across Highway 1), and Cypress Provincial Park / Cypress Mountain (north, up Cypress Bowl Road).

Where the stock sits: detached houses on RS2/RS3/RS5 streets, semi-detached strata homes on Chippendale Road, and one new mixed-form project — Hawksley, on Uplands Way in the Rodgers Creek CD3 pocket. Future Cypress Village land west of Cypress Bowl Road is not yet built stock.

West Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage in Jared's FVR + GVR September 2026 reports — no West Vancouver section, sub-area rows or community medians exist for it, and no other stats source is substituted.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 256 (Whitby Estates / Park Royal), a community shuttle, runs via Chippendale Road to Westhill at the edge of this area, then via 21st Street, Gordon Avenue, 22nd Street and Marine Drive to Park Royal. No TransLink route up Cypress Bowl Road to the ski area is documented in the timetables read; BC Parks states the resort runs a free shuttle between Lot 3B and the downhill and nordic areas in ski season. Cypress Bowl Road is the access road for the residential area and the provincial park; Chippendale Road, Uplands Way and Rodgers Creek Lane serve the residential streets; Highway 1 connects east to North Vancouver and west to Horseshoe Bay. This is a car-based area.

Schools: SD45 catchments are address-based, with elementary (K–7) and secondary (8–12) schools only and no middle tier. Cypress Park Primary (IB PYP), Kindergarten to Grade 3, 4355 Marine Drive, is the school physically named for the Cypress Park area at the foot of the slope — a K–3 primary school, not a full K–7 catchment elementary for an Upper Lands address. Which of SD45's three secondary schools (Rockridge Secondary, Sentinel Secondary at 1250 Chartwell Drive, West Vancouver Secondary at 1750 Mathers Avenue) serves a Cypress Park Estates address is not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Form B diligence (the Hawksley strata, and Chippendale Mews if its strata is confirmed on title): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a new building like Hawksley, establish first whether the unit is a developer sale (disclosure statement route) or a resale (Form B route) — the diligence package differs.

Fee-simple and bare-land forms: The pocket's RS-street houses are fee-simple houses, and its bare-land strata houses DO sit in a strata — bare-land strata owners hold a Form B diligence route for the strata's common affairs even though the lot carries a house; the title, not the built form, decides.

District plans and zoning — West Vancouver's own pair only: District of West Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 4985, 2018, and Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 — never White Rock's Bylaw 2506 / 2220 pair, which belongs to White Rock only. Zoning here uses RS2, RS3 and RS5 single-family zones, CD3 for Rodgers Creek (density set by lot-size band), and the CV (Cypress Village) Zone created by Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024. The OCP names Cypress Village and Cypress West as future neighbourhoods in the Upper Lands.

SSMUH as the District states it: the bylaw's ground-oriented dwelling rules, carried in the British Properties research, state 4 dwellings maximum per lot, and 6 maximum if the site is wholly or partly within 400 metres of a prescribed bus stop — a house-lot rule that shapes the RS streets, not the strata complexes themselves.

Hazard permits — the defining checks on this slope: a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface, and the District's Community Wildfire Resiliency Plan describes the Cypress Park area as consistently sloped terrain with Cypress Falls Park to the east and the planned Cypress Village west of Cypress Bowl Road. An Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank — Cypress Creek and Rodgers Creek both run through the area — and a subdivision can trigger a difficult-terrain development permit on steep terrain. These apply to strata alterations and landscaping at Hawksley and Chippendale Mews, not just to house lots.

Hawksley's listings say Cypress Park Estates; its count says British Properties.

3900 Cypress Bowl Road falls outside the SD45 locator's listed ranges for Cypress Bowl Road (Even 3850–3850, Odd 3755–3757) — a listing that names a catchment school for an Upper Lands home is stating something the district's own tool does not confirm.
Rodgers Creek's growth cap is a fixed number: 974 homes (researched Nov 1, 2026).

The new building's own numbers do not agree with each other yet (checked Nov 1, 2026). Hawksley appears as 57 condos + 7 townhomes in its presale source and as a 72-unit development in other project and listing sources, at two different Uplands Way addresses, with build years of 2025 and 2026 both in print — early-days documentation for a brand-new building is exactly why the strata plan and disclosure / Form B, not marketing pages, govern a purchase here.

items.t: Established Upper Lands lots: single-family homes on Chippendale Road, Uplands Way, Woodgreen Drive and the Rodgers Creek streets, in RS2, RS3 and RS5 single-family zones (Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010, Sections 202, 203 and 205), including British Pacific Properties subdivisions of single-family parcels on Uplands Way and at the end of Chippendale Road under the Cypress Village (CV) Zone as the District's development-applications record states them — built lot fabric, documented as such, not a lot offering.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Boundaries are not verified as an exact line — District planning sources place the area above Highway 1, below the 1,200-foot contour, with the Rodgers Creek area east of Cypress Bowl Road and the Cypress Village planning area west of Cypress Bowl Road.

Nearby areas: Rodgers Creek and the British Properties / Chartwell (east and south-east), Whitby Estates and Westhill (south, below Highway 1), Caulfeild (south-west, across Highway 1), and Cypress Provincial Park / Cypress Mountain (north, up Cypress Bowl Road).

Parks and trails: Cypress Falls Park is a District park in the area, with waterfalls, Cypress Creek and designated off-leash trails (listed RS2 and Dedicated in the District Parks Master Plan); Cypress Trails Park (RS3 and Dedicated) and Woodburn Park are also District parks in the area — all three are District parks, distinct from Cypress Park (Cypress Provincial Park), where Cypress Mountain Resort sits and BC Parks maintains the Bowen Lookout, Black Mountain Plateau and Hollyburn Peak backcountry trails. Recreation: West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive in Ambleside; library: West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive. Health care: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver; North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre, Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade. Shopping: a grocery store or shopping centre inside the residential area is not verified (none confirmed); the District plan for the future Cypress Village anticipates neighbourhood shopping, a school and a community centre inside that future village — planned amenities, not existing ones.

Roads and transit: Cypress Bowl Road is the access road for the residential area and for Cypress Provincial Park; Chippendale Road, Uplands Way and Rodgers Creek Lane serve the residential streets; Highway 1 connects east to North Vancouver and the Lions Gate Bridge route to Vancouver and west to Horseshoe Bay and Highway 99. TransLink route 256 (Whitby Estates / Park Royal), a community shuttle, runs via Chippendale Road to Westhill at the edge of this area, then via 21st Street, Gordon Avenue, 22nd Street and Marine Drive to Park Royal. No TransLink route up Cypress Bowl Road to the ski area is documented in the timetables read — BC Parks states the resort runs a free shuttle between Lot 3B and the downhill and nordic areas in ski season.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Cypress Park Estates

items.t: Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010: RS2, RS3 and RS5 single-family zones with the Section 200 minimum-site-area ladder in; CD3 for Rodgers Creek, with density set by lot-size band (Sections 601–603); and the CV (Cypress Village) Zone (Section 750) for Cypress Village. Secondary suites and a detached secondary suite are permitted uses in the single-family zones under the bylaw's ground-oriented rules, and secondary suites must be registered with the District.

Hazard Development Permits (District frame — the live Cypress checks): a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface — the defining check here, on consistently sloped terrain per the District's Community Wildfire Resiliency Plan; an Environmental Development Permit for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank (Cypress Creek and Rodgers Creek both run through the area); and the Foreshore Development Permit Area frame for waterfront property at risk of coastal flooding, as the District states it.

Strata block (applies to the built Rodgers Creek strata; no bare-land strata stock is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Cypress Park Estates ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cypress Park Estates

items.t: The Upper Lands growth is zoned, not rumoured: Cypress Village has its own CV Zone created by Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024, and its first works are a numbered District permit (DP 24-115) — a seller's "village coming" claim can be checked against the District's development-applications page, permit by permit.

Three District parks sit inside the residential area: Cypress Falls Park, Cypress Trails Park and Woodburn Park are District parks here — distinct from the provincial park up the road that shares the Cypress name, a confusion the District's own Parks Master Plan listings keep separate (RS2/Dedicated; RS3/Dedicated).

The Guinness history is District record: the District history page states a British group led by the Guinness family purchased most of the Upper Lands above this area, began to build the British Properties, and built the Lions Gate Bridge — the development lineage behind the Rodgers Creek / Uplands parcels. A District account of the "Cypress Park Estates" name itself is not verified.

items.t: New construction homes for sale in Cypress Park Estates, West Vancouver

faq.a: It is the MLS site/area name for the Upper Lands pocket on Cypress Bowl Road, Chippendale Road and Uplands Way. District sources use Cypress Park, Rodgers Creek and the Uplands instead, and Cypress Village / Cypress West are the OCP's future neighbourhoods. It is not Cypress Mountain or the provincial park.
faq.q: Is Cypress Park Estates a real neighbourhood?

faq.a: One building: Hawksley on Uplands Way — freehold strata apartment/condo units (and 7 townhomes) by British Pacific Properties with Beedie Living, listed as built 2026. Everything else verified in the pocket is houses, semi-detached strata homes (Chippendale Mews), or unbuilt projects.
faq.q: What condos can I actually buy here today?

faq.a: Neither, yet — both conflicts are not confirmed. Address: 3271–3281 Uplands Way (presale source) vs 3963 Uplands Way (current MLS listings). Count: 57 condominiums + 7 townhomes (presale source) vs a "72-unit" description in two other sources. Verify the civic address, strata plan number and total lots on the title and Form B / disclosure statement for the specific unit.
faq.q: Hawksley's address and unit count differ between sources — which do I trust?

faq.a: Listings state built 2026, so the building is complete; a unit still held by the developer is a new-home sale (5% GST, REDMA rescission on the original contract, Newly Built Home PTT Exemption may apply), while a unit resold by an owner is a resale (Form B route, no GST). Establish which seller you are dealing with first.
faq.q: Is a Hawksley purchase a presale or a resale, and does GST apply?

faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in BC since November 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw; check the filed bylaws.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Hawksley condo long-term?

faq.a: The total is not confirmed: the presale source counts 57 condominiums plus 7 townhomes; a project report calls it a 72-unit condominium building. Listings use the civic address 3963 Uplands Way (presale marketing used 3271–3281 Uplands Way) and classify the subdivision as Cypress Park Estates — it is Uplands/Rodgers Creek product above Highway 1.
faq.q: How many homes are in Hawksley, and where is it really?

faq.a: No — Chippendale Mews is recorded, from the developer's site, as semi-detached strata homes on Chippendale Road: ground-oriented strata houses, a different form, maintenance profile and buyer pool from Hawksley's townhomes, and its unit count, year and restrictions are not confirmed on any independent source.
faq.q: Are Chippendale Mews units townhouses I can compare with Hawksley?

faq.a: No. The residential area is in the District of West Vancouver on and below Cypress Bowl Road, while BC Parks states Cypress Mountain Resort is entirely within Cypress Park (Cypress Provincial Park), reached by Cypress Bowl Road from Highway 1.
faq.q: Is Cypress Park Estates the same place as Cypress Mountain?

faq.a: TransLink's 256 shuttle serves Chippendale Road at Westhill at the edge of the residential area and runs to Park Royal; no TransLink route up Cypress Bowl Road is documented in the timetables, and BC Parks states the resort runs a free shuttle between Lot 3B and the downhill and nordic areas in ski season.
faq.q: Is there a bus to Cypress Mountain or to Park Royal?

faq.a: The District's Area Development Plan for Cypress Village and Eagleridge plans a new community west of Cypress Bowl Road with housing, employment space and community amenities; Council paired it with Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 5206, 2024, initial works are under Development Permit 24-115 to British Pacific Properties Limited, and the Eagleridge lands transferred to the District were dedicated as park.
